item.title: Saijo Sake: Brewed with Ishizuchi's Water — Guide
item.description: Saijo, a city at the foot of Mount Ishizuchi in eastern Ehime, is celebrated as a town of water. Pure snowmelt and rainfall from the sacred mountain filter down through the ground and rise back up all over the city as ‘uchinuki’, free-flowing artesian spring water so clean and abundant that residents draw it for drinking and cooking from spouts around town. This exceptional soft water is the foundation of Saijo’s sake brewing: local breweries use it to produce clean, refined sake much prized in the region.

item.title: Izu Wasabi Farms: Japan's Finest Wasabi in Spring-Fed Terraces — Guide
item.description: The mountain valleys of the Izu Peninsula are one of Japan’s premier wasabi-growing regions, the plant cultivated in terraced stone beds through which cold, pure spring water flows constantly, a traditional method recognised as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System. Real fresh wasabi, grated to order from the root, is aromatic and gently sweet, a world away from the fiery horseradish paste most people know, and valley farms and roadside shops offer tastings, freshly grated wasabi over rice, and the region’s beloved novelty: wasabi ice cream.
